questions.q: In the context of shopping and personal finance, items that are absolutely essential for human survival, such as food, basic clothing, and shelter, are classified as:
questions.explain: **Needs** are goods or services that are required for a human being to survive. Without them, life or basic health is threatened.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: What is the fundamental difference between a consumer's **needs** and **wants**?
options: Needs are purchased with cash, while wants are purchased on credit.
Needs are essential for survival, while wants are mere desires that make life more comfortable.
Needs are always expensive, whereas wants are cheap and affordable.
Needs apply only to adults, while wants apply only to children.
questions.explain: The core difference is based on necessity. **Needs** (like water and basic food) are compulsory for survival, whereas **wants** (like designer shoes or video games) simply improve the standard of living but are not life-threatening if missed.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When applying sound shopping tips to make a purchasing decision with a limited budget, a wise consumer should:
options: Buy all their wants first and borrow money for their needs.
Satisfy their needs first before considering their wants.
Purchase items randomly as they walk through the market.
Ignore both needs and wants to save all the money.
questions.explain: Due to the economic reality of limited resources, making smart decisions requires consumers to prioritize their necessities (**needs**) over their desires (**wants**).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: The spontaneous and unplanned decision to buy a product just before or at the exact moment of payment is referred to as:
questions.explain: **Impulse buying** occurs when a consumer suddenly decides to buy something they did not originally plan to purchase, often triggered by emotions, attractive displays, or sales promotions.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct negative effect of impulse buying?
options: It increases the consumer's ability to save money for the future.
It ensures the consumer only buys what is absolutely necessary.
It leads to the disruption of the consumer's personal budget and financial regret.
It automatically extends the warranty period of the purchased goods.
questions.explain: A major **effect of impulse buying** is financial instability. By purchasing items not originally budgeted for, a consumer may deplete funds meant for vital needs, leading to debt and buyer's remorse (regret).
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: A formal written document provided by a manufacturer promising to repair or replace a product if it develops a fault within a specified period of time is known as a:
questions.explain: A **Warranty** is a type of after-sales service and legal guarantee that assures the buyer that the product is of good quality and will be fixed or replaced if it fails prematurely.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies

questions.q: When an electronics store sends a technician to a customer's house to securely mount and set up a newly purchased television at no extra charge, this activity is an example of:
questions.explain: Services provided to a customer *after* they have paid for and received the product—such as **installation**, home delivery, and servicing—are classified collectively as **after-sales services**.
questions.exam: BECE Business Studies: Entrepreneurial Skill, Consumer & Society
questions.subject: Business Studies
